title: NexaReach Studio
subtitle: Responsible AI for a remote marketing team
author: Syed Hassan Ahmed
framework: NIST AI RMF 1.0 + Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1)

company.locations: Pakistan, United Kingdom and United States
company.business: Fictional remote digital marketing agency providing paid advertising, creative production and customer engagement.
company.benefit: Use AI to shorten drafting and support workflows while keeping customer data, campaign decisions and public claims under human control.
company.boundary: All company details, observations, risk ratings and approvals are fictional. This is a portfolio simulation, not a client engagement or assurance opinion.

systems.oversight: Marketing reviewer checks every public output

systems.provider: Illustrative enterprise provider - not yet selected

systems.affected: Customers and campaign owners; Consumers and clients; Clients and support users

gaps.observation: No named AI risk owner or approval route in assumed interviews.
gaps.target: AI charter, accountable owners and release authority

gaps.observation: Tool list omits owners, inputs, affected people and intended limits.
gaps.target: Four use-case records with lifecycle and review triggers

gaps.observation: Personal AI accounts allowed; no AI-specific onboarding material.
gaps.target: Approved-tool register, acceptable use and training

gaps.observation: General confidentiality policy exists; no prompt-data classification.
gaps.target: Minimize inputs, block restricted data and verify retention

gaps.observation: Assumed procurement folder lacks AI training and deletion terms.
gaps.target: Vendor review covering reuse, hosting, deletion and subprocessors

gaps.observation: MFA exists on email; AI and freelancer access not centrally governed.
gaps.target: SSO/MFA, managed endpoints and scoped time-limited access

gaps.observation: Ad reviews are informal; no model-output approval record.
gaps.target: Independent approval bound to the exact output revision

gaps.observation: Workflow proposal allows broad CRM and advertising connector scopes.
gaps.target: Read-only connectors; deny payments and spend changes

gaps.observation: No review of proxy attributes, consent scope or exclusion effects.
gaps.target: Ban sensitive targeting; contextual fairness and consent review

gaps.observation: Creative assets have no recorded rights or synthetic-media review.
gaps.target: Rights checks, required disclosure and verified payment callbacks

gaps.observation: No repeatable AI test set, version baseline or complaint monitoring.
gaps.target: Release tests, weekly sampling and change-triggered re-evaluation

gaps.observation: Generic incident plan has no AI pause, recall or vendor deletion steps.
gaps.target: AI playbook, kill switch, appeals and decommission checklist

risks.name: Client data leaks to an AI service
risks.event: Remote staff paste a client contact list into an AI tool; customer information is retained or exposed.
risks.why: Frequent AI use and no prompt controls make exposure plausible; personal-data impact stays severe.
risks.response: Approved enterprise tools, input minimization, restricted-data gate and retention review
risks.proof: Verified data-flow review, DLP tests and supplier retention settings

risks.name: Remote AI or ad account takeover
risks.event: A stolen freelancer session grants access to campaign or AI workspaces.
risks.affected: Clients, remote workers and the agency
risks.why: Distributed identities and uneven MFA expand exposure; stolen sessions can still cause major harm.
risks.response: SSO, phishing-resistant MFA, managed devices, least privilege and rapid revocation
risks.proof: IdP/endpoint evidence and access revocation drill

risks.name: Prompt injection triggers unsafe actions
risks.event: Untrusted lead or web text instructs the assistant to disclose data or misuse connectors.
risks.why: External text is routinely processed; isolated tools reduce opportunity, not the consequence of a bypass.
risks.response: Treat external text as data, constrain connectors and gate external actions
risks.proof: Adversarial end-to-end model/connector tests; not demonstrated by metadata simulation

risks.name: Fabricated claims reach customers
risks.event: AI invents a product guarantee or policy that is published or repeated by support.
risks.why: Generative outputs can be inaccurate; reviewed source material and sign-off lower likelihood.
risks.response: Approved source material, independent fact checks, human release and escalation
risks.proof: Claim-verification sample and revision-bound publication approvals

risks.name: Unfair or intrusive audience targeting
risks.event: Lead labels infer sensitive characteristics and exclude or manipulate groups.
risks.why: Proxy attributes can bias categories; harm remains material even after review.
risks.response: Prohibit sensitive profiling; review consent, proxies and subgroup outcomes
risks.proof: Use-case impact review with affected-user input and representative test data

risks.name: Supplier reuses or transfers client inputs
risks.event: An unreviewed supplier trains on prompts or stores client data in an unexpected region.
risks.why: Supplier terms and subprocessors are unknown; contractual and technical checks reduce exposure.
risks.response: Review processing roles, training opt-out, locations, deletion and exit terms
risks.proof: Signed terms, settings export and documented transfer assessment where applicable

risks.name: Unlicensed or misleading synthetic creative
risks.event: Generated assets copy protected work or depict a person without permission.
risks.affected: Rights holders, depicted people and consumers
risks.why: Creative provenance is currently absent; documented review reduces avoidable release errors.
risks.response: Rights/provenance checklist, likeness consent and contextual disclosure
risks.proof: Asset rights log and documented synthetic-media release review

risks.name: Deepfake instruction causes payment fraud
risks.event: A synthetic executive voice persuades a remote employee to change a payee.
risks.why: Remote requests can impersonate leaders; known-channel callback and dual approval reduce likelihood.
risks.response: AI cannot pay; independently verify payee changes and require dual authorization
risks.proof: Finance control walkthrough and callback tabletop

risks.name: Shadow AI bypasses governance
risks.event: Staff use personal tools outside the inventory to process client work.
risks.why: Tool sprawl is assumed common; training and sanctioned access reduce but do not eliminate bypass.
risks.response: Approved tools, easy request route, training and proportionate access monitoring
risks.proof: Inventory reconciliation and access/training coverage report

risks.name: AI outage or runaway workflow disrupts delivery
risks.event: A provider failure or repeated tool loop delays support and consumes unexpected budget.
risks.why: External service dependency is material; quotas and manual fallback limit frequency of disruption.
risks.response: Usage caps, circuit breaker, human fallback and tested disable/retire process
risks.proof: Quota/circuit-breaker logs, outage exercise and recovery verification

functions.name: GOVERN
functions.text: AI charter, tool approval, training, supplier criteria and escalation authority.

functions.name: MAP
functions.text: Four-system inventory, intended limits, input routes, affected groups and harm scenarios.

functions.name: MEASURE
functions.text: Risk scoring, repeatable policy checks, release criteria and a monitoring specification.

functions.name: MANAGE
functions.text: Prioritized owners and deadlines, risk acceptance rules, AI incident response and retirement.

metrics.definition: Inventoried AI systems / discovered AI systems
Public releases with valid revision-bound sign-off / public releases

metrics.target: 0; any event pauses the affected flow

metrics.definition: Source-supported answers / 50 sampled FAQ answers; 0 critical false claims
metrics.frequency: Before release, weekly and on changes

metrics.definition: In-scope campaigns with consent/proxy/subgroup review / in-scope campaigns
Minutes from validated alert to disabled affected AI integration
metrics.target: At most 15 minutes in a drill
